title: Hawaii Island Salvation Army pantries report staple shortages after Lala
summary_or_snippet: Big Island Now reported that Salvation Army food pantries in Hilo, Honokaa, and Kona needed donations because staple supplies were low after Lala-related pressure. The pantries normally distribute about 75 to 150 food bags during weekly distributions at each site, and the Hilo corps reported 20 new families seeking help.

title: Eastport's only full-size grocery store remains without a committed reopening
summary_or_snippet: The Portland Press Herald reported that R&M IGA Foodliner closed after its owner retired and had been the only full-size grocery serving Eastport and the Pleasant Point reservation. Passamaquoddy voters rejected a purchase due-diligence proposal, and without a reopening commitment residents would need to drive about 35 minutes or more to Calais for full-service grocery access.

title: Puerto Rico water shutoffs add food-preparation and prepared-food costs
summary_or_snippet: The Guardian reported unreliable water service and rotating shutoffs in Puerto Rico, including more than 180,000 homes without public access to potable water during 48-hour shutoff cycles. The Food Line relevance is the reported burden on cooking and household budgets, including residents spending more time and money on water and prepared food.

title: Texas SNAP redetermination delays interrupted benefits for an East Texas household
summary_or_snippet: The Texas Tribune reported that Texas SNAP redetermination timeliness fell from 83 percent in January to 28 percent in July. The article also documented an East Texas household whose benefits did not arrive after a timely reapplication, leading the family to rely on food banks that sometimes did not have enough food.
